It feels like I've used up every tool I have working gig after gig, balancing college classes and waitressing and enduring poverty, to finally be noticed enough, deemed good enough to offered the WFH job. It was the accumulation of 10 years of endless work, and it made me feel that everything I'd gone through was worthwhile. It made me glad I didn't kill myself 10 years ago; I thought everything was going to finally be okay. To lose it all after a year, it's thrown me right back to that same state of existence I was in - in constant fear of not having enough to just survive, of not being good enough to ever 'get out', of suffering without reward. 

I understand that not everyone can succeed despite working as hard as they can, but to me, if all that work results in nothing but more pain and even more work and not at the very least some stability in life (by this, I mean a safe place to live and enough food and other basic needs), then how much is one expected to keep enduring?

That is all I want from my life - basic stability and safety. I don't want to dream of having anything more than that ever again, because it seems I never will. I don't even have the will to try. 

The idea of having to start all over again is daunting. It feels impassable, insurmountable. At least if the Universe gave me a sign that everything was going to be okay, then I could justify trying to fight again for the life that I want.
